stem: Best guess: which entity's income is taxed twice when distributed to owners?

choices.explanation: Correct. C corporations pay entity tax, and shareholders pay tax on dividends.

explanation: C corporations pay entity tax, and shareholders pay tax on dividends.

stem: A C corporation earns $100 of taxable income and distributes everything left as a qualified dividend to a shareholder who pays 20% plus 3.8% NIIT. What is the combined tax?

choices.explanation: That's the top individual rate on pass-through income.

stem: An LLC with one individual member makes no election. How is it taxed?

choices.text: As a C corporation by default
choices.explanation: Default for a single-member LLC is disregarded.
Correct. Reg. §301.7701-3(b): single-owner eligible entities default to disregarded status.
A partnership needs two or more owners.

explanation: Reg. §301.7701-3(b): single-owner eligible entities default to disregarded status.

stem: Founders plan to reinvest all profits for 8 years and then sell the company's stock. Which entity likely produces the lowest tax?

choices.text: C corporation, possibly with the §1202 exclusion
choices.explanation: Correct. Retained profits bear only 21%, and qualifying stock gain may be excluded under §1202.

choices.text: Partnership, because there is one level of tax
choices.explanation: Owners are taxed on reinvested profits every year at up to 37%.

choices.text: S corporation, to avoid double taxation
choices.explanation: Same annual pass-through tax on reinvested profits and no §1202.

choices.text: Sole proprietorship owned by one founder
choices.explanation: Unlimited liability and the full individual rate on reinvested profits.

explanation: Retained profits bear only 21%, and qualifying stock gain may be excluded under §1202.

stem: Which fact would prevent a business from operating as an S corporation?

choices.text: Its shareholders are all U.S. citizens
It has voting and nonvoting common stock
A VC partnership will buy preferred stock
choices.explanation: Correct. Partnership shareholders and a second class of stock (preferred) both violate S requirements.

explanation: Partnership shareholders and a second class of stock (preferred) both violate S requirements.

stem: A new business expects large losses for 3 years and its owners have high income from other active businesses where they will materially participate. Which entity best uses the losses?

choices.text: C corporation, to retain the losses

choices.explanation: PHC status is a penalty-tax trap, not an entity choice.
Correct. Pass-through losses flow to owners, subject to basis, at-risk, passive, and excess business loss limits.

explanation: Pass-through losses flow to owners, subject to basis, at-risk, passive, and excess business loss limits.

stem: An LLC with two members wants to be taxed as an S corporation. What must it do?

choices.text: Nothing, because LLCs are S corporations by default
Reincorporate as a corporation under state law
File Form 2553, which also elects association status
choices.explanation: Correct. An eligible entity that timely files Form 2553 is deemed to have elected to be an association.

explanation: An eligible entity that timely files Form 2553 is deemed to have elected to be an association.

stem: An owner in the 32% bracket runs a profitable service business as a sole proprietorship with $150,000 of net earnings. Which change most likely reduces self-employment/payroll taxes?

choices.text: Convert to an S corporation and pay a reasonable salary
choices.explanation: Correct. S corporation distributions above reasonable wages aren't subject to payroll or SE tax.

choices.text: Form a single-member LLC with no election
choices.explanation: Still a disregarded entity subject to SE tax.

choices.text: Form a general partnership with a spouse
choices.explanation: General partners pay SE tax on their shares.

choices.text: Increase the owner's draws during the year

explanation: S corporation distributions above reasonable wages aren't subject to payroll or SE tax.

stem: An investor acquired qualified small business stock at original issue in 2018 (basis $1 million) and sells it in 2025 for $9 million. How much gain can she exclude?

choices.explanation: The exclusion is 100% for stock acquired after September 27, 2010.
The stock was held more than 5 years.
Correct. 100% of the gain, within the greater of $10 million or 10 × basis.

explanation: §1202: 100% exclusion for pre-July 5, 2025 stock held more than 5 years, capped at the greater of $10 million or 10 × basis.
reviewNote: Uses a One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21) amount or effective date. Verify against current IRS guidance and exam materials.

stem: What is the maximum combined federal rate on C corporation income that is distributed as a qualified dividend to a top-bracket shareholder subject to NIIT?

choices.explanation: Adds the rates without reducing the base.
That's the top individual ordinary rate.

stem: A two-member LLC taxed as a partnership changed to corporate classification by election in 2023. When can it generally elect to change classification again?

choices.explanation: Correct. Reg. §301.7701-3(c)(1)(iv): 60-month limitation after an elective change.
It can change after 60 months (or with IRS consent).

explanation: Reg. §301.7701-3(c)(1)(iv): 60-month limitation after an elective change.

stem: Owners of a pass-through expect to sell the business's assets in 5 years. Why might a buyer prefer to buy the assets of an S corporation instead of the stock of a C corporation?

choices.text: The buyer gets stepped-up asset basis, no double tax
choices.explanation: Correct. An asset purchase steps up basis; for a pass-through, the gain is taxed once at the owner level.

choices.text: Stock purchases give the buyer a stepped-up basis
choices.explanation: A stock purchase keeps the old inside basis.

choices.text: C corporations can't sell their assets directly
choices.explanation: They can, but double tax applies.

choices.text: S corporation asset sales are always tax-free
choices.explanation: Gain passes through and is taxed once.

explanation: An asset purchase steps up basis; for a pass-through, the gain is taxed once at the owner level.

stem: Which entity allows owners to specially allocate depreciation to one owner and increase basis for entity-level debt?

choices.explanation: No special allocations; entity debt doesn't create shareholder basis.
A sole proprietorship has only one owner.
Correct. §704(b) special allocations and §752 liability sharing are partnership features.

explanation: §704(b) special allocations and §752 liability sharing are partnership features.

stem: Which owner can claim the §199A QBI deduction on business income?

choices.text: A C corporation shareholder on dividends

explanation: The QBI deduction is available to individuals, trusts and estates on qualified income from pass-throughs, not to C corporations.

stem: An owner wants employer-paid health insurance excluded from her income. Which entity provides that for an owner-employee?

choices.explanation: Correct. C corporation shareholder-employees can exclude it.

choices.text: An S corporation, as a 50% owner

explanation: Shareholder-employees of a C corporation can receive tax-free health benefits; partners and more-than-2% S shareholders can't.

stem: A venture capital fund organized as a partnership plans to buy shares in a startup. Which entity should the startup be?

choices.explanation: Correct. Partnerships can't hold S corporation stock.

explanation: S corporation shareholders must be individuals, estates or certain trusts and exempt organizations; partnerships are ineligible.

stem: How is a single-member LLC classified by default for federal tax purposes?

choices.explanation: Correct. It's treated like a sole proprietorship.

explanation: Under check-the-box rules, a single-member LLC is disregarded unless it elects corporate classification.

stem: An owner wants to withdraw each year's profits with only one level of federal income tax and no SE tax on distributions. Which entity fits best?

choices.explanation: Correct. Distributions avoid SE tax, with reasonable salary.

explanation: S corporation income is taxed once; distributions (beyond reasonable compensation) aren't subject to SE or payroll taxes.

stem: An investor holds QSBS issued in August 2025 for 4 years and sells at a gain. What exclusion applies?
explanation: For QSBS issued after July 4, 2025, the exclusion is 50% after 3 years, 75% after 4 and 100% after 5 years.

stem: An owner will distribute all profits and qualifies for the full QBI deduction at the top bracket. Which structure gives the lower combined federal income tax rate?

choices.text: A C corporation with no salary

explanation: A C corporation's 21% plus 23.8% on dividends is about 39.8%; 37% with a 20% QBI deduction is about 29.6%.

stem: A C corporation converts to S status. Its assets have built-in gains. When is the built-in gains tax a risk?

choices.text: Only in the first S year

explanation: Built-in gains recognized within 5 years after conversion are taxed at the corporate level.

stem: Investors expect large depreciation losses from a property financed with nonrecourse debt. Which entity best lets them use the losses?

choices.explanation: Shareholders get no basis for entity debt.
Correct. Partners' basis includes entity debt.

explanation: Partners include their share of partnership liabilities in basis; S shareholders don't include corporate debt.

stem: What federal rate applies to a personal service C corporation's taxable income?

choices.explanation: Correct. The flat corporate rate applies.
That flat PSC rate was repealed.

explanation: Personal service corporations pay the same flat 21% rate as other C corporations.

stem: A sole proprietor with $200,000 of profit forms an S corporation and pays herself a $90,000 reasonable salary. Ignoring the SE tax deduction, about how much employment tax does she save? (2025 wage base $176,100.)

choices.explanation: Correct. SE tax ≈ $27,190 versus payroll tax of $13,770 on salary.
Payroll tax is still due on salary.

stem: A C corporation with large accumulated E&P and mostly rental and interest income plans to elect S status. What is the main tax risk?

choices.explanation: Correct. Excess passive investment income with E&P triggers tax and, after 3 years, termination.

choices.text: Double tax on all of its income
No risk at all from the election

explanation: An S corporation with C-corporation E&P and passive income above 25% of gross receipts faces the ENPI tax and possible termination.

stem: A foreign individual investor wants to own part of a U.S. operating business with pass-through taxation. Which entity works?

choices.explanation: Correct. Nonresident aliens can't own S corporation stock.

explanation: A partnership-taxed LLC allows foreign owners; S corporations don't.

stem: What is the rate of the qualified business income deduction?
explanation: The §199A deduction is generally 20% of qualified business income, now permanent.

stem: What is the 2025 taxable income threshold where QBI wage and SSTB limits begin for a single filer?
explanation: For 2025, the QBI limits phase in above $197,300 (single) and $394,600 (joint).

stem: Which entity can't have a nonresident alien owner?

choices.text: An LLC taxed as a partnership

choices.explanation: Correct. Nonresident aliens are ineligible shareholders.

explanation: S corporation shareholders must be U.S. citizens or residents, certain trusts or estates.

stem: A C corporation earns $100,000 and distributes all after-tax profit as a qualified dividend to an owner taxed at 23.8%. What is the total tax?
explanation: C corporation earnings are taxed at the entity level and again as dividends.

stem: An S corporation earns $100,000 before salary. The owner takes a $60,000 reasonable salary. What are total FICA taxes on the salary (employer and employee)?
explanation: S corporation distributions aren't subject to payroll tax; reasonable salary is.

stem: A sole proprietor has $100,000 of net profit. What self-employment tax applies?

choices.explanation: That is only half of it.

explanation: SE tax applies 15.3% to 92.35% of net SE earnings up to the wage base.

stem: A single taxpayer has $80,000 of QBI and $90,000 of taxable income before the QBI deduction, with no capital gains. What is the deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. Lesser of 20% of QBI or 20% of taxable income.

explanation: Below the threshold, the deduction is the lesser of 20% of QBI or 20% of taxable income less net capital gain.

stem: QBI is $100,000, but taxable income before the QBI deduction is $70,000. What is the deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. Limited to 20% of taxable income.

explanation: The QBI deduction can't exceed 20% of taxable income (less net capital gain).

stem: A non-SSTB owner above the phase-in range has $500,000 of QBI, $100,000 of W-2 wages and no qualified property. What is the deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. 50% of W-2 wages is less than 20% of QBI.

explanation: Above the range, the deduction is limited to the greater of 50% of wages or 25% of wages plus 2.5% of UBIA.

stem: Above the range, QBI is $400,000. W-2 wages are $60,000, and UBIA of qualified property is $1,000,000. What is the deduction?
explanation: The limit is the greater of 50% of wages or 25% of wages plus 2.5% of UBIA.

stem: A single consultant (an SSTB) has 2025 taxable income well above the phase-in range. What QBI deduction applies?

choices.explanation: Correct. SSTBs lose the deduction above the range.

explanation: Specified service businesses get no QBI deduction once taxable income exceeds the phase-in range.

stem: An S corporation pays $50,000 of elective pass-through entity tax to its state. What is the federal effect for its owner?

choices.explanation: Correct. PTET is deducted at the entity level.

explanation: PTET is deductible by the entity, reducing owners' income outside the SALT cap.

stem: A C corporation elects S status when an asset has a $300,000 FMV and a $200,000 basis. It sells the asset for $350,000 in year 3. What built-in gains tax applies?

choices.explanation: Only the built-in gain at conversion.

explanation: Gain built in at conversion and recognized within 5 years is taxed at 21% at the entity level.

stem: A single-member LLC makes no entity election. How is it classified?

choices.explanation: Correct. It's treated as part of its owner.

explanation: A single-member LLC is disregarded by default unless it elects corporate status.

stem: A two-member LLC wants to be taxed as a corporation. What must it file?
explanation: An eligible entity elects corporate classification on Form 8832 (or Form 2553 for S status, which deems it).

stem: An LLC taxed as a partnership wants to allocate all depreciation to one member. Is this allowed?

choices.explanation: Correct. Special allocations must have it.

explanation: Partnership special allocations are respected if they have substantial economic effect.

stem: Founders plan to reinvest all earnings and sell the company after 6 years. Which entity may offer the biggest tax benefit?

choices.explanation: Correct. §1202 can exclude gain on sale.

explanation: Qualified small business stock in a C corporation can exclude gain on sale, up to the cap.

stem: A business wants foreign investors and several classes of preferred equity. Which entity should it avoid?

choices.explanation: Correct. It allows one class and no NRAs.

choices.text: An LLC taxed as a partnership

explanation: S corporations are limited to one class of stock and eligible shareholders.

stem: A startup expects large losses for 3 years, and its investors want to use them. Which structure fits?

choices.text: An LLC taxed as a partnership

explanation: Partnerships pass losses through, with flexible allocations, subject to basis and other limits.

stem: An S corporation owner pays herself a $10,000 salary and takes $200,000 of distributions. What is the main risk?

choices.explanation: That is not the main risk.

explanation: Unreasonably low salary invites reclassification of distributions as wages subject to payroll tax.

stem: A high-income lawyer's practice is an SSTB above the QBI phase-in range. What should drive the entity choice?
explanation: When QBI is unavailable, payroll tax savings and state PTET benefits drive the choice.

stem: Owners expect to sell appreciated business assets later. Why might an LLC beat a C corporation?

choices.explanation: Correct. One level of tax applies.

choices.text: A larger DRD for the owners

explanation: Asset sales by a C corporation and liquidation produce two levels of tax; partnerships pay one.
